notes: Anthropic source: published pricing (claude-api skill catalog, cached 2026-06-24).

OpenAI source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching, both read 2026-09-13. Note platform.openai.com/docs/pricing now redirects there.

Cache multipliers are expressed as multiples of the model's own base input rate, and are per-vendor because the terms genuinely differ. Anthropic: read 0.1x, write 1.25x at the 5-minute TTL and 2x at the hour. OpenAI: read 0.1x uniformly, and no charge at all to write a cache entry — until GPT-5.6, which introduced a 1.25x write charge. That is a per-model override rather than a vendor-wide rule.
Claude Code leans on 1h ephemeral caching, so the 5m/1h split is tracked separately rather than assumed. Codex reports a single undifferentiated cache-write figure, which is charged at the 5m rate.

OpenAI has no TTL tiers — its cache lifetime is 30 minutes from the last write or reuse, with one write rate. The write5m and write1h fields therefore carry the SAME value on every OpenAI entry: it is one rate expressed in a two-field shape Anthropic needs, not a second sourced figure. Both are 1.25x input on GPT-5.6 and 0 before it.

Not modelled: OpenAI bills 2x input and 1.5x output on any request whose input exceeds 272k tokens. Codex sessions observed here run a 258,400-token context window and turn inputs around 100k, so the threshold is not reached. Revisit if either changes.

models.why: Promotional rate, guaranteed by OpenAI only through 2026-11-21. Re-check after that date.

unknownModels.note: Models observed in local logs but absent from the published catalog. Priced at their apparent tier and flagged in the UI rather than silently guessed.

entries.why: Present in local session logs; not in the published pricing catalog as of 2026-07-27. Opus-tier pricing assumed.
